newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's ANC holds line on fiscal discipline.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's ANC holds line on fiscal discipline.

text.p: South Africa's ruling African National Congress (ANC) has resisted pressure from its labour and communist allies to relax fiscal discipline in favour of growth, but has agreed to set up a joint committee on economic strategy.

Political sources said there was no consensus on economic policy between the ANC, the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) and the South African Communist Party (SACP) at a leadership summit in Johannesburg on Thursday.

A Cosatu source said the ANC delegation, including President Nelson Mandela and Finance Minister Trevor Manuel, defended its market-friendly, macro-economic strategy for growth, employment and redistribution, known as GEAR.
The GEAR strategy commits the government to reducing the budget deficit from 5.1 percent in fiscal 1996/97 to three percent of gross domestic product by the end of the century.

"Our sense is that the ANC is not giving up on GEAR," the Cosatu source said. "We will have to convince the ANC that aspects of the GEAR are affecting delivery - aspects such as the deficit reduction programme."
Party officials said a six-member committee would examine options that could be put to leaders of the three groups at a follow-up summit in June.
ANC and Cosatu sources said there was no question that GEAR would be abandoned or radically rewritten, but labour and the communists will press for a revision of some GEAR targets.
The ANC's partners have argued throughout the first three years of democratic rule that deficit targets should be relaxed to promote job creation through accelerated economic growth.
The ANC, Cosatu and the SACP fought apartheid together and formed a formal alliance ahead of the country's first democratic elections in April 1994. The alliance won almost 62 percent of the vote.
The SACP and Cosatu hold seats in the National Assembly and the cabinet, but complain that they are not adequately consulted on government policy.

"A frank, forthright discussion was held on broad strategic perspectives, on the role of the state, on government, alliance relations, on the broad transformation process and on a shared programme of action for the alliance," the three said in a joint statement on Friday.
Cosatu and SACP sources said there was also stiff discussion about the ANC's alleged failure to consult its partners on policy formulation.

"We are partners with the ANC in this alliance. Why should we have to lobby government in the same way as business, who are not part of any alliance, to get our policies considered?" asked one source.
The alliance, which is managed by a permanent secretariat, agreed to have a leadership meeting at least twice a year in future to review policies and strategies.
